newsitem.title: NIGERIA: U.N. mission says Nigeria-Cameroon visit useful.
newsitem.headline: U.N. mission says Nigeria-Cameroon visit useful.

text.p: The head of a United Nations team looking into a territorial dispute between Nigeria and Cameroon said on Monday his visit to the region had been useful and might help reduce tension.
Omar Alim told Reuters by telephone from the Nigerian capital Abuja that his team met military ruler General Sani Abacha on Sunday after a tour of the disputed Bakassi peninsula.
"My visit to the two countries has been extremely useful in terms of soliciting measures to decrease tension," Alim said.
"I will make recommendations to the (U.N.) Secretary-General of specific measures that can be taken. I cannot say what they are right now."
The team arrived in Nigeria on Wednesday and toured Abana and Ibaka on the peninsula in the oil-rich Gulf of Guinea at the weekend.
Nigerian troops in the disputed territory are stationed on the two islands, which together with several others make up Bakassi peninsula.
Last week Nigerian foreign minister Tom Ikimi accused Cameroon of mounting attacks during the four-member team's visit. Cameroon denied the accusation.
"I saw no evidence of fighting in Bakassi, but then I was not close to the front lines," Alim said.
The U.N. team is to return to Cameroon on Monday, Alim said.
The two African nations have clashed sporadically on Bakassi with heavy loss of lives on both sides.
Both sides have troops entrenched in the impoverished islands whose inhabitants are mainly fishermen and speak Efik, the language of southeastern Nigeria.
Cameroon took its case to the World Court in 1994 but the court's ruling in March forbidding further fighting did not prevent clashes a month later.
